An Explainable AI Approach to Detecting Linguistic Markers of Mental Health Risk in Toxic Online Discourse
Online aggression, including cyberbullying and hate speech, is a significant public health concern, contributing to adverse mental health outcomes such as depression, anxiety, and suicidal ideation among social media users, and typically manifests in subtle and context-sensitive forms, such as sarcasm, emojis, and coded messages. These offensive remarks currently plague machine learning-based detection models since they are founded on one-layer linguistic features and have low interpretability.
